messages:
emily: Customer opened a ticket — intermittent 502s from /v1/embeddings. They provided a curl that sets X-Client-Req: 0x7f9c and a timestamp. No request_id in response headers. Can someone hunt server logs by that header value?

tarik: Can you paste the exact curl and the response body/headers they saw? sometimes proxies strip headers.

emily: Paste of their curl: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Client-Req: 0x7f9c" -d '{"input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings`
Response snippet: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` body: `{"error":"upstream_error"}` headers they copied: `content-type: application/json` (no request-id).

michael: OK — we can try looking for the `X-Client-Req` value in access logs. Note that header names are normalized in our logs as `x_client_req`. Hot logs retained ~14 days, cold/archived up to 90 days. Make sure the ticket timeframe is within that.

lina: customer timestamp says 2025-01-12T18:03:11Z — that should be within hot window. I'll try a quick Kibana query.

lina: Kibana query I used: `service:api AND request.path:/v1/embeddings AND http.response.status_code:502 AND headers.x_client_req:"0x7f9c"`

opsbot: search-job submitted (job id: sj-20250112-1789). Results pending, may take a minute.

lina: Found 3 hits across edge and origin. One of the hits shows an upstream timeout from the model pool: `upstream_error: read timeout` and includes our internal `req_id: rq_3a9f5b2c`.

emily: Perfect — add that req_id to the support ticket and ask if they can reproduce with a curl that includes `Prefer: return=request_id` (we add request_id to responses when present). Also ask them to grab the full debug bundle with `--verbose`.

tarik: For handoff to infra: search by internal `req_id` in hot logs: KQL snippet: `req_id:rq_3a9f5b2c OR parent_req:rq_3a9f5b2c` or direct grep in ES: `{"query":{"term":{"req_id.keyword":"rq_3a9f5b2c"}}}`. If you can't find it in hot, check archived shards; file export might be required.

michael: Note for the SRE oncall — the error path shows repeated 504s in the same 10s window and a model backend reported high error rate. If this is related to capacity, we should check Dedicated pool health for region us-west-2 around that timestamp.

emily: I'll update the customer: share internal req_id (rq_3a9f5b2c), ask for a reproduce curl with `X-Client-Req` plus `-v`, and request a debug bundle (they can run `curl -v ... -o resp.txt && tar czf debug_bundle.tgz resp.txt`). Also mention we will follow up after infra checks the pool. :thumbsup:

lina: Opsbot returned the raw log link: https://logs.redwood.internal/kibana/app/discover#/?_a=(query:(match_all:()))&id=sj-20250112-1789 — included to cross-check.

opsbot: deployment note: there was a minor model rollout at 2025-01-12T17:59:00Z affecting embedding-encoder-v2 in us-west-2. Rolling back would affect all customers — flagging infra.

tarik: For retention: remind the ticket the hot logs are 14 days; after that we need legal/archival export. Also include instruction for support engineers to request `debugbundle` via support UI which collects client headers and response bodies for us.

emily: Thanks — adding everything to the ticket and tagging @infra-oncall. Will bump if we get a repro.

michael: If infra needs me to correlate GPU metrics, ping me. I can pull pod logs and nvidia-smi timeline for the 3 reqs.

emily: closing the loop here — customer asked for ETA; I'll say we're investigating and expect an update in 2 hours after infra checks.
